raw_response:
I've been working this land for 40 years. I don't need a pamphlet to tell me what to do — I know this soil, I know the wells, I know what the market in Quzhou will take. Let me think through how I'll arrange things this year.

**My land:**
My 16.9 mu is split the way it's always been. The bulk — about 12 mu — runs wheat in the cold months and maize in the hot months, back and forth, the way my mother farmed and her mother before her. Then I keep about 2 mu in chili and the remaining 2.9 mu in cotton. The chili and cotton are what puts real money in my pocket.

**Wheat (12 mu, winter):**
I'll plough it properly before sowing in October — rotary isn't enough, the soil needs to be turned. I'll buy the improved seed from the county seed station, same variety I've used for years, it performs well here. Irrigation four times: once before sowing to settle the seedbed, once in winter to protect roots from freezing, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. I'll spray twice — once for rust and once for aphids near heading. Fertilizer I'll apply heavy on the nitrogen upfront at sowing and again at jointing. Expect around 420 jin per mu.

**Maize (12 mu, summer):**
Right after wheat harvest in June I'll rotary-till and get the hybrid seed in the ground fast. I've always used the hybrid — everyone here does now, the yield difference is real. Three irrigations: at emergence, at tasseling, and at grain fill. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer and armyworm. I push the nitrogen because summer maize responds to it. Aim for 550 jin per mu.

**Chili (2 mu, spring-summer):**
I grow my own transplants from seed I saved from last year's best plants. My family knows the local variety, buyers know it, I'm not switching. Chili drinks water and attracts every pest around, so I'll irrigate five times and spray four times — mostly for blight and aphids. I fertilize more carefully here because chili burns easily. I want 350 jin per mu of dried chili.

**Cotton (2.9 mu, spring-summer):**
Cotton is labor-intensive but I know it. I'll use the improved seed from the village supply store — not the old open-pollinated type. I'll rotary-till, sow in late April when soil is warm enough. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll setting most critically — four irrigations total. I'll spray five times; cotton pest pressure here is real, boll weevil, bollworm, spider mites. I expect around 270 jin of seed cotton per mu.
